bull.b: Very low leverage limits interest obligations and solvency pressure, giving NervGen greater financial flexibility while it funds clinical development and manages the volatility typical of an early-stage biotech.

The stronger cash balance can support ongoing trials and corporate operations over the next several months, reducing immediate liquidity pressure even though continued development spending remains substantial.

A focused lead program may concentrate limited resources around a potentially differentiated nervous-system repair opportunity, while the broader neurological applicability could provide future development options if clinical evidence supports it.

bear.b: Without product revenue, NervGen has no recurring commercial cash inflow to offset research and administrative costs. Widening losses indicate that financial performance remains dependent on successful development and future external funding.

Persistently negative and worsening operating cash flow shortens the period that existing resources can fund operations. This raises the likelihood of additional financing before commercialization and increases execution risk around the clinical program.

Regular access to equity markets provides funding flexibility but can dilute existing holders as shares are issued. The large warrant liability also adds financial complexity and may increase uncertainty around the capital structure.
